summary: The owner-approved remediation is a minimal, coherent dependency/toolchain update that resolves all three previously reachable vulnerabilities. No in-scope security finding, hardcoded credential, unintended product change, unrelated dependency selection, or deployment pin inconsistency was found. This approval covers the remediation only; full integration and final acceptance remain pending.

scope.result: The complete tracked diff was inspected. The additional decisions/telemetry modifications and untracked QA acceptance artifacts record the preceding failed freeze-qa phase; they contain no product or acceptance-harness source change. The remediation itself changes only the requested dependency, toolchain, CI/release/Docker, and documentation pins.

commands.result: x/text v0.41.0 directly requires x/sync v0.22.0, confirming that the go.sum-only x/sync update is transitive and expected.

commands.command: Heuristic sensitive-value scan of the eight remediation files and original QA report, plus manual diff review
commands.result: Scanned 9 files with 0 potential secret assignments. No private key, access key, hardcoded credential, or sensitive evidence value was found. Existing CI credentials remain GitHub secret references and were not reproduced.

verification.dependency_and_behavior_review: The only module requirement change is x/text v0.39.0 to v0.41.0. Checksum changes are confined to x/text and its transitive x/sync v0.22.0 requirement. No direct dependency was added, removed, or otherwise upgraded. Go language/toolchain directives move together from 1.25.0/go1.25.13 to 1.26.0/go1.26.10. No product source, runtime command, image entry point, final Alpine image, or acceptance-harness source was changed.
verification.workflow_release_review: Default CI, release tests, release setup-go, cache keys, download URLs, and the Docker builder consistently select Go 1.26.10. The Go 1.26.0 language directive and documentation's Go 1.26+ minimum are compatible with that exact toolchain. The release job still depends on the test job, including its vulnerability gate.
verification.evidence_hygiene: The original QA report parsed as valid JSON. Its sensitive-value scan and the remediation diff review found no exposed secret. This report contains only sanitized command results and public vulnerability metadata.
verification.residual_non_reachable_observation: govulncheck -show verbose ./... independently confirmed zero symbol-level and zero additional package-level findings. It lists GO-2026-6859 in stdlib@go1.26.10, fixed in go1.26.11, only at module level and explicitly states that project code is unaffected. No affected net/http server/MaxBytesReader call path was identified, so there is no concrete project attack vector and this is not recorded as a finding or a blocker.
verification.deferred_verification: Full integration, fresh freeze-qa, and final acceptance were not rerun by this security review and remain required after review/commit as planned.
